rationale.conceptual: The method is a custom integration of established but non-trivial techniques: coarse-grained polymer modeling, reverse mapping, MD with a specific force field (CVFF), static deformation energy-difference calculations, and micromechanics models (Mori-Tanaka, effective interface). It requires genuine understanding of polymer physics, elastic constants, and Eshelby-based micromechanics. The solver must correctly derive and implement the equations, which qualifies as a 'custom method needing genuine understanding; several interacting components; non-trivial math to translate into code'.
rationale.execution: The pipeline has many stages: (1) coarse-grained model and Monte Carlo, (2) reverse mapping, (3) MD equilibration for six systems (200 ps each) using LAMMPS with CVFF force field, (4) static deformation runs to compute elastic constants, (5) Mori-Tanaka equations, (6) effective interface model solving, (7) radius-dependent predictions over 10-10000 Å. Setting up the different systems, ensuring correct force field parameters, running multiple MD simulations, and handling the data flow from MD to micromechanics models constitutes a long, fragile orchestration with several load-bearing handoffs.

difficulty.reasoning: The paper describes a multi-scale modeling pipeline combining coarse-grained Monte Carlo, reverse mapping to atomistic detail, MD equilibration with the CVFF force field, static deformation elastic constant computations, and two micromechanics models. Reproducing the full workflow from scratch requires genuine understanding of molecular simulation and continuum mechanics, careful implementation of several non-trivial steps, and orchestration of a multi-stage pipeline. The reference solve.sh writes pre-computed paper values, but a genuine agent implementation must execute the real pipeline, which is conceptually deep and executionally complex.

compute_estimate.reasoning: The MD simulations involve small systems (a few thousand atoms) and short trajectories (200 ps), easily handled on a modern CPU with minimal memory. The rest of the pipeline is purely numeric with negligible memory. Data volume is essentially zero.
